title: Blackstone, Banks Amass $60 Billion for Broadcom's AI Chip Deal
key_facts: Bloomberg says Broadcom's Wall Street banks are starting to gather $60 billion of new financing for AI chips, to benefit Anthropic and other companies.
Banks are poised to send out letters to investors for a $42 billion Class A senior-secured tranche (the first-in-line slice of the debt).
Blackstone is leading an $18 billion Class B junior tranche and is committing $9 billion from various funds, planning to sell on the rest.
The deal has yet to be announced; the sources asked not to be named; a Broadcom representative declined to comment.
Bloomberg says the financing has been taking shape for weeks and is watched as a test of whether investors still want to back the AI buildout amid public backlash against data-center construction.
Broadcom wants to sell more chips and data-center equipment and challenge Nvidia; Anthropic needs ever more computing capacity.
In August, Nvidia announced a partnership with six big finance names, including Blackstone, to mobilize more than $500 billion for AI.
quote_evidence: Broadcom Inc.'s Wall Street syndicate are starting to gather $60 billion of fresh AI chip financing to benefit Anthropic PBC and other companies, according to people with knowledge of the matter.
Blackstone Inc. is leading an $18 billion tranche of Class B junior debt, committing $9 billion from various funds with plans to syndicate the rest, the people said.

Banks involved in the massive debt package are poised to send out syndication letters for a $42 billion Class A senior-secured tranche, the people said, asking not to be identified discussing the deal, which has yet to be announced.
why_it_matters_hint: The financing is watched as reassurance that investors still want to fund AI's buildout despite public backlash against data centers.
event_date: 2 Oct 2026 (Bloomberg report; financing not yet announced). Follow-up of 1 Oct 2026 Reuters report that Broadcom would lend Anthropic up to $42 billion to lease its chips.
